feature.title: B0 capture: many sessions per server start, and skip warm-up forwards in the integrity check

brief.goal: Make the B0 capture serve blocks of sessions per server start (default 25), with per-block capture files, warm_start marking, block-level retry and resume, and a manifest that records the session-to-block mapping. Make b0_integrity.py skip and separately count the server's no-request warm-up verify forwards, and read both the new block layout and F100's one-session-per-dir layout.
criteria: `b0_capture.py OUT --block N` (default 25) serves the sessions without DONE.json in blocks of up to N, one server start per block. Each session in a block goes to the same server one after another, through its own `run_capture_sessions.py --session-ids <sid>` call, with max-running-requests left at 1. The capture files (trace.jsonl, router.*, router.res.*, verify-accept, metrics.jsonl, server.log) land under OUT/blocks/<block-id>/. results.jsonl, rids.json, drive-samples.jsonl (session_start/session_end samples around that session's runner call) and DONE.json stay under OUT/<sid>/. DONE.json names its block and carries warm_start. warm_start is true exactly for the first session served after each server start, including the first session of a re-served block. Such sessions are kept, not dropped.

A block whose server never becomes healthy, dies, or fails the block-level checks (capture_verify.check_capture, residency_complete) is re-served once under a new block id. Only its sessions without DONE.json are re-served. A session whose results_complete fails gets no DONE but does not fail the rest of its block. Sessions still without DONE after the retry move to OUT/failed/<sid>/FAILED.json and are listed in the outcome and the manifest, as today. A rerun skips sessions with DONE.json or FAILED.json, regroups the rest into blocks with fresh block ids, and never overwrites an existing block dir. `--pilot K` serves the first K sampled sessions as one block and writes no manifest.

manifest.json (schema bumped to 2) lists the done sessions, a session -> block mapping, the warm_start sessions, and the blocks with their residency header identity check and their file sizes/sha256. It still lists split, failed, flagged, rows and validity_rule. OUT/rids.json is still the merge of the per-session rids.json files. Each block dir also holds a rids.json for its own sessions.

b0_integrity.py excludes verify forwards whose route-log `rids` is empty from the route, snapshot and label checks and from missing-record counting. It reports them as `no_request_forwards`, which is never in _FAILING. A synthetic session with two such forwards whose captured gate input is zero and whose ids are all 0 passes with ok=true and no_request_forwards == 2.

b0_integrity.py accepts as positional arguments both a block dir with many sessions and an F100 session dir. With a rids.json in the dir, it adds `by_session` (per session_id, with split) and keeps by_stratum and by_horizon. A rid missing from rids.json is reported, not crashed on. Existing tests in test_b0_integrity.py still pass.

DSV41_REFERENCE.md section 33.25 describes the block layout (OUT/blocks/<block-id>/, per-session dirs, DONE.json's block and warm_start), --block, the block retry and resume rule, the manifest's session -> block mapping, and integrity's no_request_forwards and block-dir arguments. Any corpus numbers stay 'not run by the gate' or `pending`.
rules: Change only analysis/dsv41-drive/prefetch-replay/{b0_capture.py,b0_integrity.py,b0_manifest.py}, their tests test_b0_capture.py, test_b0_integrity.py and test_b0_manifest.py (extend them; no new test dirs), and DSV41_REFERENCE.md section 33.25. Do not change python/sglang/**, run_capture_sessions.py, capture_verify.py, tier_sim.py, b0_guards.py or b0_split.py.

Tests are CPU only and never start a server. Drive b0_capture's orchestration through injected callables, as capture_all(serve=..., check=...) does today: give the block driver injectable start/serve-session/stop/check functions so tests can simulate a server death, a block-check failure and a per-session failure. Build b0_integrity fixtures with the existing _trace/_router/_residency helpers in test_b0_integrity.py and extend them (for example a rids=[] forward with zero x and zero ids).

Every pytest check goes through `/Users/dnikolaidis/.hx/checks/divix01-pytest <files> -q -p no:randomly` from the checkout root, naming the test files only. Laptop checks are limited to `python3 -m py_compile <files>`. Never write uv run, uv sync or pip install. Workers never run anything on divix01 and never start a capture. Production stays stopped, and the full capture is the owner's to start.

Keep b0_capture.main's order: refuse_launch (b0_guards) before any lock or server, then run_locks.take(DISK_LOCK), then run_locks.take(arm_env.GPU_LOCK), held across all blocks. Start the server as _serve_session does today (taskset SERVER_CORES, start_new_session=True, capture_verify._healthy with arm_env.DSPARK_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_S). Stop it only with capture_verify.stop_server after the block's last session, so the ring files are complete before the block checks run.
server_env takes the block dir (trace/router/verify-accept/metrics under it). recipe_env and the residency switch stay unchanged, and test_the_server_env_* keeps passing against a block dir.

Session identity comes from rid_map / rids.json (`<sid>-t<turn>` -> session_id, turn, split), exactly as run_capture_sessions.py names rids. Sessions in one block have distinct rids, so pass no --rid-suffix. b0_integrity maps a forward to a session through its `rids` and the capture dir's rids.json; with max-running-requests 1 a verify forward has at most one session.

Style (.claude/rules/general-code-style.md, comment-style.md, no-dataclasses.md, no-getattr-defensive.md): small pure keyword-arg functions under ~100 LOC, with orchestration that reads like pseudocode. Use msgspec.Struct for any new container (b0_integrity already uses msgspec.Struct Joined), and no getattr/hasattr defensively. Comments are 1-2 ASCII lines stating facts, with no history. Rewrite the module docstrings of b0_capture.py, b0_integrity.py and b0_manifest.py for the block layout.

Errors keep today's split. Completeness failures raise one of b0_capture._COMPLETENESS_ERRORS (RuntimeError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError) and are caught per attempt. Integrity failures are counters listed in _FAILING. no_request_forwards is a plain count outside _FAILING.
decisions: Blocks of --block sessions per server start (default 25, so 12 starts for 300 sessions). Sessions are served sequentially on one server with max-running-requests 1, as both_cpu_ab serves many sessions per server.
Capture files are per block under OUT/blocks/<block-id>/. Per-session outputs (results.jsonl, rids.json, drive-samples.jsonl, DONE.json) stay under the session dir, and DONE.json names its block.
The first session served after each server start is marked warm_start=true in its DONE.json and in the manifest, and is kept, not dropped.
Resume: sessions with DONE.json are skipped and the remaining ones are regrouped into blocks.
A block whose server dies or whose completeness check fails is re-served once, covering only its sessions without DONE. Sessions still failing go to failed/ and are listed, as today.
drive_flags per session still come from drive samples taken around each session.
Every b0_guards refusal and the disk-then-GPU lock order stay. --pilot K means the first K sessions in one block, with no manifest.
b0_manifest records the session -> block mapping and the warm_start flags.

b0_integrity skips verify forwards with no rids in the route, snapshot and label checks and reports them as no_request_forwards, never as a failure. It reads both the block layout (per-session and per-stratum reporting through rids.json) and F100's one-session-per-dir layout.

No serving code changes. Tests sit beside the scripts in the existing test_b0_*.py files. DSV41_REFERENCE 33.25's recipe text is updated for the block layout and warm_start. The full capture is started by the owner afterwards, not by a check.

Early stop (owner, 2026-10-12): the run stops early only after 2 blocks in a row whose retry also left every one of their sessions without DONE (a systematic fault); otherwise it keeps serving blocks. The per-session '5 failed in a row' rule is replaced by this.

Re-served block dir (owner, 2026-10-12): when a block is re-served, the first attempt's block dir is kept in place if any of its sessions got DONE.json (their capture lives there); if none did, it is moved to OUT/failed/blocks/<block-id>/. Nothing is deleted, and sessions with DONE are never re-served.
questions: Today the run stops after 5 sessions fail in a row. With blocks, one bad server start fails up to 25 sessions at once. What should stop the run early?
When a block is re-served, what happens to the first attempt's block dir?

Keep the per-session rule: stop after 5 failed sessions in a row, in serving order
Never stop early; serve every block and report

Always move it to failed/blocks/<block-id>/ and re-serve every session of the block, including those that passed
Delete it when no session in it is DONE

tasks.title: Block driver: grouping, block retry, warm_start, resume and quarantine in b0_capture
tasks.intent: Replace the one-session-per-server loop (capture_all and serve_with_retry) with capture_blocks. It groups the sessions that lack DONE/FAILED into blocks of block_size and gives each block a fresh id under OUT/blocks/ (never reusing an existing dir in blocks/ or failed/blocks/). For each block it calls start, then serve_session for each session in order, then stop, then check_block, then check_session for each session. Only after both checks pass does it write per-session rids.json and DONE.json {session_id, block, warm_start, attempts, summary}, plus <block>/rids.json. warm_start is true for the first session served after each start. A failed block attempt (start raising, check_block raising) is re-served once under a new block id, covering only sessions without DONE. Sessions still failing after that go to OUT/failed/<sid>/FAILED.json. Two Brief open questions are settled with the recommended answers. (Q1) The run stops after 2 consecutive blocks whose retry left every session failed. (Q2) A failed block dir is kept if any of its sessions got DONE; otherwise it moves to OUT/failed/blocks/<id>. All CPU tests use injected fakes.
tasks.produces: b0_capture.BLOCKS_DIR = "blocks"; DEFAULT_BLOCK = 25. capture_blocks(*, out_dir: str, sessions: list[dict], split: dict, block_size: int, start, serve_session, stop, check_block, check_session) -> dict, returning {"done": [sid], "failed": [sid], "blocks": {sid: block_id}, "warm_start": [sid]}, where blocks and warm_start cover done sessions, including those done in earlier runs (read back from their DONE.json). The callables are: start(block_dir: str) -> handle (raises on an unhealthy server); serve_session(handle, session: dict, session_dir: str, block_dir: str) -> None (raises on runner failure; the session dir already exists and is clean); stop(handle) -> None (always called, in a finally); check_block(block_dir: str) -> dict summary (raises one of _COMPLETENESS_ERRORS); check_session(session: dict, session_dir: str) -> None (raises). DONE.json is {session_id, block, warm_start, attempts, summary: check_block's summary}. Each block dir gets rids.json, the rid_map union of its sessions.

tasks.title: Server lifecycle, block checks, --block and _finish in b0_capture
tasks.intent: Split _serve_session into _start_server(block_dir), which writes server.log in the block dir, waits for health under taskset SERVER_CORES and raises if the server never becomes healthy, and _serve_one(handle, session, session_dir, block_dir). _serve_one writes session.jsonl and session_start/session_end drive samples into the session dir and runs run_capture_sessions.py --session-ids sid with results in the session dir; it uses no --rid-suffix. stop is capture_verify.stop_server. Split check_complete into a block check (capture_verify.check_capture plus residency_complete on the block dir) and a session check (results_complete). server_env takes the block dir. main gains --block (default DEFAULT_BLOCK), and --pilot K becomes the first K sessions with block_size=K. main keeps refuse_launch before the locks and the disk-then-GPU lock order. _finish passes the outcome's blocks and warm_start into write_manifest and keeps the merged OUT/rids.json. Rewrite the module docstring for the block layout.
tasks.produces: b0_capture.main([OUT, --block N, --pilot K, --sessions, --seed, --max-tokens]). The server's capture files are under OUT/blocks/<id>/, and per-session outputs are under OUT/<sid>/.

tasks.title: Manifest schema 2: blocks, session -> block mapping, warm_start
tasks.intent: Rewrite b0_manifest for the block layout. Residency headers are now read from block dirs under corpus_dir/blocks/ (one *.snap.bin prefix per block), and all blocks must agree on rows and validity_rule. sessions is the sorted list of mapped done sessions. The file table covers each listed block dir and each done session dir. Bump MANIFEST_SCHEMA to 2 and add the fields "blocks" (block_id -> [sid]), "session_block" (sid -> block_id) and "warm_start". A block dir that holds no done session is not listed. Extend test_b0_manifest.py to the block layout.

It reads block headers from corpus_dir/blocks/<block_id>/ and raises ValueError on an empty mapping or on block headers that disagree. MANIFEST_SCHEMA = 2.

tasks.title: Integrity: skip no-request verify forwards, count no_request_forwards
tasks.intent: In b0_integrity._join, a verify graph forward whose route-log rids is empty (the server's warm-up verifies, seq 5 and 6 in the pilot) is counted as no_request_forwards and left out of the joined set. It therefore never reaches the route, snapshot or label checks or missing_router/missing_label. no_request_forwards stays out of _FAILING. Add a test: a session with two rids=[] verify forwards whose captured x and ids are all zero passes with ok and no_request_forwards == 2, and the real forwards are still checked.
tasks.produces: check_session reports include the integer key no_request_forwards (set through _join's counts, with += so the key exists whenever there is a verify forward). It is not in _FAILING.

tasks.title: Integrity: block-dir layout and by_session reporting through rids.json
tasks.intent: Make b0_integrity accept both a block dir (many sessions) and an F100 session dir as positional arguments. When the dir holds rids.json, check_session also reports by_session (session_id -> counts and rates, with split). It splits the joined forwards by each forward's rids through rids.json, and reports a rid missing from rids.json under unmapped_rids instead of crashing. by_stratum and by_horizon are unchanged. _summarize aggregates per_session across dirs and sums no_request_forwards. check_session setdefaults no_request_forwards to 0. Rewrite the module docstring (layouts, no_request_forwards, by_session).
tasks.produces: check_session(out_dir, *, W, bias, residency_prefix=RESIDENCY_PREFIX) -> report with by_session when out_dir/rids.json exists. main(MODEL_PATH, DIR...) takes block or session dirs.

tasks.title: B0 capture driver: blocks of sessions per server start, manifest schema 2, and the 33.25 recipe
tasks.intent: T1 (block orchestration), T2 (server lifecycle, checks, main/_finish) and T3 (manifest) are one contract: capture_blocks' outcome {done, failed, blocks, warm_start} flows through _finish into write_manifest, and the on-disk layout under OUT/blocks/<id>/ and OUT/<sid>/ must match what b0_manifest reads. T6 documents that same layout and recipe, so one reviewer checks the text against the code. Review load 4+2+2+1 = 9.
tasks.focus: Check that the ring files are complete before the block checks: stop (capture_verify.stop_server) must run in a finally after the block's last session and before check_block. Check that refuse_launch still runs before any lock, that DISK_LOCK is taken before GPU_LOCK and held across all blocks, and that no serving code was touched. Check that warm_start is true exactly for the first session after each server start, including on a re-served block. In the retry: only sessions without DONE are re-served, under a fresh block id; existing block dirs are never overwritten or wiped while they hold DONE sessions' capture; an empty failed block moves to failed/blocks/<id>; quarantine goes to failed/<sid>/FAILED.json; the run stops after 2 consecutive all-failed blocks. On resume: DONE/FAILED sessions are skipped, earlier DONE sessions' block and warm_start are read back into the outcome, and the rest are regrouped. --pilot K serves one block of K and writes no manifest. Drive samples bracket each session's runner call, and drive_flags still reads per-session drive-samples.jsonl. Rids are not suffixed. The manifest takes headers from block dirs, requires all blocks to agree, lists only blocks with done sessions, and its file table covers block and session dirs. MANIFEST_SCHEMA is 2. 33.25 matches the code (--block default 25, the retry and stop rules, the session -> block mapping) and leaves numbers 'not run by the gate'/pending. Tests use injected fakes only and never start a server.

tasks.title: b0_integrity: skip no-request warm-up verifies, read block dirs with per-session reporting
tasks.intent: Both change b0_integrity.py's reading of a capture dir: T4 filters what _join admits, and T5 changes what check_session/_summarize report per dir and per session. One reviewer, one module, and the same synthetic fixtures in test_b0_integrity.py. Review load 1+2 = 3.
tasks.focus: Check that forwards with rids == [] are left out of the route, snapshot, label and missing-record counts, and only of those: a real forward with a missing record must still fail. no_request_forwards is never in _FAILING, defaults to 0, and is summed by _summarize. by_session splits joined forwards through rids.json, with each forward assigned to exactly one session (max-running-requests 1). Unmapped rids are reported, not raised. by_stratum and by_horizon totals are unchanged. F100 single-session dirs without rids.json still work, and the existing tests pass unchanged. The rewritten module docstring matches the behaviour.
